name: Jeatrai
title: Levitical singer in the temple
summary: Jeatrai was a Levite from the family of Gershon mentioned in the genealogical records of Chronicles. He was part of the Levitical families appointed for service in the temple, especially connected to singing and musical duties. His significance lies in his place within the Levitical lineage that served in God's house.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of the Gershonite family
keyEvents.description: Jeatrai is listed in the genealogical register of the Levites from the Gershonite family as part of the Levitical service order.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Levitical service
keyEvents.description: As a Levite, Jeatrai belonged to the tribe appointed for service in the tabernacle and later in the temple.

keyEvents.title: The heritage of the Gershonite family
keyEvents.description: The Gershonite family, to which Jeatrai belonged, was one of the three main branches of the tribe of Levi and had specific duties in worship.

keyEvents.title: Levitical cities and places of service
keyEvents.description: The Levites, including the family of Gershon, were given cities to live in among the other tribes of Israel, ensuring their service throughout the land.
